population.span: We enrolled 7868 women between the ages of 60 and 90 years who had a bone mineral density T score of less than -2.5 but not less than -4.0 at the lumbar spine or total hip.

endpoint.span: Secondary end points included nonvertebral and hip fractures.

estimate.span: Denosumab also reduced the risk of nonvertebral fracture, with a cumulative incidence of 6.5% in the denosumab group, versus 8.0% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.95; P=0.01)

analysis_set.span: POPULATION: Full analysis set (all randomized participants)

treatment_strategy.span: Subjects were randomly assigned to receive either 60 mg of denosumab or placebo subcutaneously every 6 months for 36 months.

follow_up.span: TIME FRAME: 36 months | POPULATION: Full analysis set (all randomized participants)

entry_population_matches_question.why: Women aged 60-90 with BMD T score < -2.5 (osteoporosis) in a trial titled for postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, randomised denosumab vs placebo.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Denosumab for prevention of fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis.

notes: Served HR 0.8 (0.67-0.95) equals the abstract's HR 0.80 (0.67 to 0.95) for nonvertebral fracture. Analysis set and follow-up are registry spans (NCT00089791 result outcome 1, which reports the same HR 0.8, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.95, Cox regression, with counts Placebo=293/3906, Denosumab=238/3902). The served_outcome estimand is RR but served_estimand is HR and the row is an HR, so the row is internally consistent; mixing it with RR rows on the page would be a scale mix. The page question concerns vertebral fractures; nonvertebral fracture is a secondary endpoint of this trial. The europepmc_core.json abstract is truncated and lacks this sentence.
